sanskrit: vīkṣamāṇas tato laṅkāṃ kapiḥ kṛtamanorathaḥ vardhamānasamutsāhaḥ kāryaśeṣam acintayat
english: Then the monkey, his desire fulfilled, his enthusiasm growing, gazed upon Laṅkā and reflected on what remained yet to be done.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu khalv aviśiṣṭaṃ me kartavyam iha sāmpratam yad eṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ bhūyaḥ saṃtāpajananaṃ bhavet
english: "What indeed remains for me to do here at present, by which further pain may be inflicted upon these rākṣasas?"

sanskrit: vanaṃ tāvat pramathitaṃ prakṛṣṭā rākṣasā hatāḥ balaikadeśaḥ kṣapitaḥ śeṣaṃ durgavināśanam
english: "The grove has been ravaged, distinguished rākṣasas have been slain, a portion of the army has been destroyed — what remains is the destruction of the fortress."

sanskrit: durge vināśite karma bhavet sukhapariśramam alpayatnena kārye 'smin mama syāt saphalaḥ śramaḥ
english: "Once the fortress is destroyed, the task will become one of pleasant effort; with little exertion in this undertaking my labour will bear fruit."

sanskrit: yo hy ayaṃ mama lāṅgūle dīpyate havyavāhanaḥ asya saṃtarpaṇaṃ nyāyyaṃ kartum ebhir gṛhottamaiḥ
english: "This fire, the carrier of oblations, blazing on my tail — it is fitting to give it satisfaction with these finest dwellings."

sanskrit: tataḥ pradīptalāṅgūlaḥ savidyud iva toyadaḥ bhavanāgreṣu laṅkāyā vicacāra mahākapiḥ
english: Then, with his tail ablaze, the great monkey moved about the rooftops of Laṅkā's mansions like a thundercloud lit by lightning.

sanskrit: mumoca hanumān agniṃ kālānalaśikhopamam
english: Hanūmān released fire whose flames were like those of the fire of universal dissolution.

sanskrit: śvasanena ca saṃyogād ativego mahābalaḥ kālāgnir iva jajvāla prāvardhata hutāśanaḥ
english: Fanned by the wind, that fire blazed with tremendous speed and great force, spreading and growing like the fire of cosmic time.

sanskrit: pradīptam agniṃ pavanas teṣu veśmasu cārayat
english: The wind drove the blazing fire through those dwellings.

sanskrit: tāni kāñcanajālāni muktāmaṇimayāni ca bhavanāny avaśīryanta ratnavanti mahānti ca
english: Those great mansions adorned with lattices of gold and set with pearls and gems collapsed and fell.

sanskrit: tāni bhagnavimānāni nipetur vasudhātale bhavanānīva siddhānām ambarāt puṇyasaṃkṣaye
english: Those shattered palaces fell to the ground like the celestial abodes of Siddhas falling from the sky at the exhaustion of their merit.

sanskrit: vajravidrumavaidūryamuktārajatasaṃhitān vicitrān bhavanād dhātūn syandamānān dadarśa saḥ
english: He beheld brilliant mineral streams flowing from the mansions — diamond, coral, vaidūrya gem, pearl, and silver, all mingled together.

sanskrit: nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ tṛṇānāṃ ca yathā tathā hanūmān rākṣasendrāṇāṃ vadhe kiṃcin na tṛpyati
english: Just as fire is never sated with wood and grass, so too Hanūmān was not in the least sated with the slaying of those lords of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: hutāśanajvālasamāvṛtā sā hatapravīrā parivṛttayodhā hanūmātaḥ krodhabalābhibhūtā babhūva śāpopahateva laṅkā
english: That Laṅkā, enveloped in the flames of fire, her champions slain, her warriors routed, overcome by the furious power of Hanūmān, appeared like a city struck down by a curse.

sanskrit: sasaṃbhramaṃ trastaviṣaṇṇarākṣasāṃ samujjvalaj jvālahutāśanāṅkitām dadarśa laṅkāṃ hanumān mahāmanāḥ svayambhukopopahatām ivāvanim
english: The great-spirited Hanūmān beheld Laṅkā, her rākṣasas terrified and distraught, blazing with the flames of fire, like the earth struck by the wrath of the Self-born Brahmā.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasāṃs tān subahūṃś ca hatvā vanaṃ ca bhaṅktvā bahupādapaṃ tat visṛjya rakṣo bhavaneṣu cāgniṃ jagāma rāmaṃ manasā mahātmā
english: Having slain those many rākṣasas, having broken that grove with its many trees, having set fire to the dwellings of the rākṣasas, that great-souled one turned his mind to Rāma.

sanskrit: laṅkāṃ samastāṃ saṃdīpya lāṅgūlāgniṃ mahākapiḥ nirvāpayām āsa tadā samudre harisattamaḥ
english: Having set all of Laṅkā ablaze, that foremost of monkeys, the best of the vānaras, then extinguished the fire of his tail in the ocean.

sanskrit: saṃdīpyamānāṃ vidhvastāṃ trastarakṣo gaṇāṃ purīm avekṣya hānumāṃl laṅkāṃ cintayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: Gazing upon the burning, devastated city of Laṅkā, her bands of rākṣasas terrified, the monkey Hanūmān fell into thought.

sanskrit: tasyābhūt sumahāṃs trāsaḥ kutsā cātmany ajāyata laṅkāṃ pradahatā karma kiṃsvit kṛtam idaṃ mayā
english: A great fear arose in him, and self-reproach was born within: "What act have I committed by burning Laṅkā?"

sanskrit: dhanyās te puruṣaśreṣṭha ye buddhyā kopam utthitam nirundhanti mahātmāno dīptam agnim ivāmbhasā
english: "Blessed are those foremost men, those great souls who restrain anger that has arisen in the mind with intelligence, as water restrains a blazing fire."

sanskrit: yadi dagdhā tv iyaṃ laṅkā nūnam āryāpi jānakī dagdhā tena mayā bhartur hataṃ kāryam ajānatā
english: "If this Laṅkā has been burned, then surely noble Jānakī too has been burned. By me, not knowing it, the task of my lord has been destroyed."

sanskrit: yad artham ayam ārambhas tat kāryam avasāditam mayā hi dahatā laṅkāṃ na sītā parirakṣitā
english: "The very purpose for which this undertaking was begun has been ruined — for in burning Laṅkā, I did not protect Sītā."

sanskrit: īṣatkāryam idaṃ kāryaṃ kṛtam āsīn na saṃśayaḥ tasya krodhābhibhūtena mayā mūlakṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "This was a small matter that needed to be done — of that there is no doubt. But overcome by anger, I have brought about its utter ruin."

sanskrit: vinaṣṭā jānakī vyaktaṃ na hy adagdhaḥ pradṛśyate laṅkāyāḥ kaś cid uddeśaḥ sarvā bhasmīkṛtā purī
english: "Jānakī is clearly destroyed — not a single spot of Laṅkā is seen unburned; the entire city has been reduced to ashes."

sanskrit: yadi tad vihataṃ kāryaṃ mayā prajñāviparyayāt ihaiva prāṇasaṃnyāso mamāpi hy atirocate
english: "If indeed this task has been ruined by my perversion of judgment, then laying down my life right here seems most fitting to me."

sanskrit: kim agnau nipatāmy adya āhosvid vaḍavāmukhe śarīram āho sattvānāṃ dadmi sāgaravāsinām
english: "Shall I fall into the fire today, or into the submarine fire? Or shall I give my body to the creatures that dwell in the ocean?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi jīvatā śakyo mayā draṣṭuṃ harīśvaraḥ tau vā puruṣaśārdūlau kāryasarvasvaghātinā
english: "How can I, who have destroyed the entirety of the task, ever look upon the lord of monkeys, or those two tiger-like men, while still alive?"

sanskrit: mayā khalu tad evedaṃ roṣadoṣāt pradarśitam prathitaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kapitam anavasthitam
english: "By me, due to the fault of rage, has been displayed what is already renowned in the three worlds — the fickleness and instability of monkeys."

sanskrit: dhig astu rājasaṃ bhāvam anīśam anavasthitam īśvareṇāpi yad rāgān mayā sītā na rakṣitā
english: "Shame upon this rājasic nature, uncontrolled and unstable, by which even I, capable of mastery, failed through passion to protect Sītā."

sanskrit: vinaṣṭāyāṃ tu sītāyāṃ tāv ubhau vinaśiṣyataḥ tayor vināśe sugrīvaḥ sabandhur vinaśiṣyati
english: "With Sītā destroyed, those two will perish as well; with their destruction Sugrīva together with his kinsmen will perish."

sanskrit: etad eva vacaḥ śrutvā bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ dharmātmā sahaśatrughnaḥ kathaṃ śakṣyati jīvitum
english: "Hearing this very news, how will the righteous-souled Bharata, ever devoted to his brothers, along with Śatrughna, be able to survive?"

sanskrit: ikṣvākuvaṃśe dharmiṣṭhe gate nāśam asaṃśayam bhaviṣyanti prajāḥ sarvāḥ śokasaṃtāpapīḍitāḥ
english: "With the most righteous Ikṣvāku lineage gone to destruction without doubt, all the subjects will be tormented by grief and anguish."

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ bhāgyarahito luptadharmārthasaṃgrahaḥ roṣadoṣaparītātmā vyaktaṃ lokavināśanaḥ
english: "Thus I, devoid of fortune, stripped of the accumulation of dharma and artha, my soul overcome by the fault of rage, am clearly the destroyer of the world."

sanskrit: iti cintayatas tasya nimittāny upapedire pūram apy upalabdhāni sākṣāt punar acintayat
english: As he was reflecting thus, favorable omens presented themselves — those he had perceived earlier — and he reconsidered.

sanskrit: atha vā cārusarvāṅgī rakṣitā svena tejasā na naśiṣyati kalyāṇī nāgnir agnau pravartate
english: "Or rather — she of beautiful limbs, that auspicious one, is protected by her own radiance and will not perish; fire does not function within fire."

sanskrit: na hi dharmān manas tasya bhāryām amitatejasaḥ svacāritrābhiguptāṃ tāṃ spraṣṭum arhati pāvakaḥ
english: "Indeed fire cannot rightfully touch, by the law of dharma, the wife of that one of boundless splendor — her who is protected by her own chastity of conduct."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ rāmaprabhāvena vaidehyāḥ sukṛtena ca yan māṃ dahanakarmāyaṃ nādahad dhavyavāhanaḥ
english: "Surely by the power of Rāma and by the merit of the princess of Videha, this fire — whose very work is burning — did not burn me."

sanskrit: trayāṇāṃ bharatādīnāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ devatā ca yā rāmasya ca manaḥkāntā sā kathaṃ vinaśiṣyati
english: "She who is the deity of the three brothers beginning with Bharata, and who is beloved of Rāma's heart — how could she perish?"

sanskrit: yad vā dahanakarmāyaṃ sarvatra prabhur avyayaḥ na me dahati lāṅgūlaṃ katham āryāṃ pradhakṣyati
english: "Or since this imperishable fire, the lord everywhere whose very work is burning, did not burn my tail — how could it scorch that noble lady?"

sanskrit: tapasā satyavākyena ananyatvāc ca bhartari api sā nirdahed agniṃ na tām agniḥ pradhakṣyati
english: "By her ascetic practice, by her truthful speech, and by her singular devotion to her husband, she could herself extinguish fire — fire will not burn her."

sanskrit: sa tathā cintayaṃs tatra devyā dharmaparigraham śuśrāva hanumān vākyaṃ cāraṇānāṃ mahātmanām
english: As he thus reflected upon the queen's embrace of dharma, the great-souled Hanūmān heard the words of the Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: aho khalu kṛtaṃ karma durviṣahyaṃ hanūmatā agniṃ visṛjatābhīkṣṇaṃ bhīmaṃ rākṣasasadmani
english: "Ah, truly a deed nearly beyond endurance has been performed by Hanūmān, who again and again unleashed fearsome fire upon the dwellings of the rākṣasas!"

sanskrit: dagdheyaṃ nagarī laṅkā sāṭṭaprākāratoraṇā jānakī na ca dagdheti vismayo 'dbhuta eva naḥ
english: "This city of Laṅkā with its watch-towers, ramparts, and gateways has been burned — yet Jānakī has not been burned. This is a wonder and marvel to us!"

sanskrit: sa nimittaiś ca dṛṣṭārthaiḥ kāraṇaiś ca mahāguṇaiḥ ṛṣivākyaiś ca hanumān abhavat prītamānasaḥ
english: By these omens of manifest import, by reasons of great virtue, and by the words of the seers, Hanūmān's heart became glad.

sanskrit: tataḥ kapiḥ prāptamanorathārthas tām akṣatāṃ rājasutāṃ viditvā pratyakṣatas tāṃ punar eva dṛṣṭvā pratiprayāṇāya matiṃ cakāra
english: Then the monkey, his desired object attained, knowing the princess to be unharmed, and having seen her again in person, resolved to set out on his return journey.

sanskrit: tatas tu śiṃśapāmūle jānakīṃ paryavasthitām abhivādyābravīd diṣṭyā paśyāmi tvām ihākṣatām
english: Then, going to Jānakī who was seated at the foot of the śiṃśapā tree, he saluted her and said: "By good fortune I see you here unharmed."

sanskrit: tatas taṃ prasthitaṃ sītā vīkṣamāṇā punaḥ punaḥ bhartṛsnehānvitaṃ vākyaṃ hanūmantam abhāṣata
english: Then Sītā, gazing again and again upon Hanūmān as he prepared to depart, spoke to him words filled with affection for her husband.

sanskrit: kāmam asya tvam evaikaḥ kāryasya parisādhane paryāptaḥ paravīraghna yaśasyas te balodayaḥ
english: "Truly, you alone are sufficient to accomplish this task. O slayer of enemy heroes, your rise of power is glorious."

sanskrit: balais tu saṃkulāṃ kṛtvā laṅkāṃ parabalārdanaḥ māṃ nayed yadi kākutsthas tasya tat sādṛśaṃ bhavet
english: "Yet if Kākutstha, the crusher of enemy armies, were to fill Laṅkā with his forces and then lead me away, that would be befitting of him."

sanskrit: tad yathā tasya vikrāntam anurūpaṃ mahātmanaḥ bhavaty āhavaśūrasya tattvam evopapādaya
english: "Bring about therefore what is truly befitting of that great-souled hero in battle — cause his valor to manifest as it rightly should."

sanskrit: tad arthopahitaṃ vākyaṃ praśritaṃ hetusaṃhitam niśamya hanumāṃs tasyā vākyam uttaram abravīt
english: Having heard those words of hers — purposeful, modest, and supported by reasons — Hanūmān spoke this reply to her.

sanskrit: kṣipram eṣyati kākutstho haryṛkṣapravarair vṛtaḥ yas te yudhi vijityārīñ śokaṃ vyapanayiṣyati
english: "Kākutstha will come swiftly, surrounded by the foremost of monkeys and bears, and having conquered your enemies in battle, he will remove your sorrow."

sanskrit: evam āśvāsya vaidehīṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ gamanāya matiṃ kṛtvā vaidehīm abhyavādayat
english: Having thus reassured the princess of Videha, Hanūmān, the son of the wind-god, made up his mind to depart and took leave of Vaidehī.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kapiśārdūlaḥ svāmisaṃdarśanotsukaḥ āruroha giriśreṣṭham ariṣṭam arimardanaḥ
english: Then that tiger among monkeys, that crusher of enemies, eager to see his lord, ascended the finest of mountains, Ariṣṭa.

sanskrit: tuṅgapadmakajuṣṭābhir nīlābhir vanarājibhiḥ sālatālāśvakarṇaiś ca vaṃśaiś ca bahubhir vṛtam
english: It was adorned with lofty rows of blue padmaka trees, and thickly set with sāla, tāla, āśvakarṇa, and many bamboo groves.

sanskrit: latāvitānair vitataiḥ puṣpavadbhir alaṃkṛtam nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ dhātuniṣyandabhūṣitam
english: It was ornamented with spreading canopies of flowering creepers, filled with herds of various beasts, and adorned with the flowing streams of mineral ores.

sanskrit: bahuprasravaṇopetaṃ śilāsaṃcayasaṃkaṭam maharṣiyakṣagandharvakiṃnaroragasevitam
english: It was endowed with many waterfalls, made difficult by accumulations of rock, and frequented by great seers, yakṣas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, and serpents.

sanskrit: latāpādapasaṃbādhaṃ siṃhākulitakandaram vyāghrasaṃghasamākīrṇaṃ svādumūlaphaladrumam
english: Its caverns were dense with creepers and trees and troubled by lions; its slopes were crowded with packs of tigers; its trees bore sweet roots and fruits.

sanskrit: tam ārurohātibalaḥ parvataṃ plavagottamaḥ rāmadarśanaśīghreṇa praharṣeṇābhicoditaḥ
english: That foremost of leaping beings, of surpassing strength, ascended that mountain, spurred on by the joy that was quickened by his eagerness to see Rāma.

sanskrit: tena pādatalākrāntā ramyeṣu girisānuṣu saghoṣāḥ samaśīryanta śilāś cūrṇīkṛtās tataḥ
english: Trodden by the soles of his feet on the beautiful mountain ridges, the rocks split apart with a loud crash and were pulverized.

sanskrit: sa tam āruhya śailendraṃ vyavardhata mahākapiḥ dakṣiṇād uttaraṃ pāraṃ prārthayaṃl lavaṇāmbhasaḥ
english: Having climbed that king of mountains, the great monkey grew in size, seeking to leap from the southern to the northern shore of the salt-sea.

sanskrit: adhiruhya tato vīraḥ parvataṃ pavanātmajaḥ dadarśa sāgaraṃ bhīmaṃ mīnoraganiṣevitam
english: Then that hero, son of the wind-god, having mounted the mountain, beheld the fearsome ocean frequented by fish and serpents.

sanskrit: sa māruta ivākāśaṃ mārutasyātmasaṃbhavaḥ prapede hariśārdūlo dakṣiṇād uttarāṃ diśam
english: That tiger among monkeys, born of the wind-god, sprang through the sky like the wind itself, traversing from south to north.

sanskrit: sa tadā pīḍitas tena kapinā parvatottamaḥ rarāsa saha tair bhūtaiḥ prāviśad vasudhātalam kampamānaiś ca śikharaiḥ patadbhir api ca drumaiḥ
english: That finest of mountains, pressed by that monkey, roared along with the beings dwelling within it and sank into the earth, its peaks trembling and its trees falling.

sanskrit: tasyoruvegān mathitāḥ pādapāḥ puṣpaśālinaḥ nipetur bhūtale rugṇāḥ śakrāyudhahatā iva
english: Churned by the speed of his thighs, flower-bearing trees were uprooted and fell to the ground, as if struck down by Indra's weapon.

sanskrit: kandarodarasaṃsthānāṃ pīḍitānāṃ mahaujasām siṃhānāṃ ninado bhīmo nabho bhindan sa śuśruve
english: The terrifying roar of mighty lions dwelling in the hollows of the caves, disturbed and afflicted, was heard splitting the sky.

sanskrit: srastavyāviddhavasanā vyākulīkṛtabhūṣaṇā vidyādharyaḥ samutpetuḥ sahasā dharaṇīdharāt
english: Vidyādharī women, their garments loosened and disheveled, their ornaments thrown into disarray, leapt suddenly from the mountain.

sanskrit: atipramāṇā balino dīptajihvā mahāviṣāḥ nipīḍitaśirogrīvā vyaveṣṭanta mahāhayaḥ
english: Enormous, powerful, blazing-tongued serpents of great venom, their heads and necks pressed down, writhed and coiled about.

sanskrit: kiṃnaroragagandharvayakṣavidyādharās tathā pīḍitaṃ taṃ nagavaraṃ tyaktvā gaganam āsthitāḥ
english: Kiṃnaras, serpents, gandharvas, yakṣas, and vidyādharas likewise, abandoning that finest of mountains as it was being crushed, took to the sky.

sanskrit: sa ca bhūmidharaḥ śrīmān balinā tena pīḍitaḥ savṛkṣaśikharodagrāḥ praviveśa rasātalam
english: And that glorious upholder of the earth, pressed by that mighty one, sank into the netherworld, its lofty peaks and trees intact.

sanskrit: daśayojanavistāras triṃśadyojanam ucchritaḥ dharaṇyāṃ samatāṃ yātaḥ sa babhūva dharādharaḥ
english: That mountain, ten yojanas in breadth and thirty yojanas in height, became level with the earth.
